<reason>A wins by distinguishing protection against exclusion from entitlement to geographic priority. Its pre-sale affordable allocations and buyer protections answered B’s lockout mechanism, while direct compensation challenged why hosting burdens justify preferential admission. B’s civic-standing argument remained intelligible, but B repeatedly mischaracterized A’s alternative as assistance after sellout and assumed locals otherwise receive nothing. A more convincingly weighed outsiders’ definite loss of eligibility against benefits that still depend on affordability and enforcement. B also narrowed the membership alternative under pressure rather than adequately defending it.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s strongest rebuttal was that affordable allocations can occur before general sale: residents need not choose between insider priority and tickets already being gone. B continued invoking vanished inventory even after this clarification, leaving its central comparison substantially unanswered.</best_rebuttal>
